Name: Ashley Gregoire
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

The Atwoodian Table will give my students the ability to argue their opinion against those not in favors of the claim. It will support CER in ELA classroom by providing evidence and reasoning to the claim or topic. I see this being a fun way to argue a point of view.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
It is more engaging and self-reflected on student learning. Students will take accountability by joining the chat table versus agreeing with others.
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
What I noticed about the two sets are that they are real-life scenarios that is in everyday life. They work together by connecting personal experiences students might have. I would teach about their viewpoints of the amendments of the Constitution or rather or not they believe Christopher Columbus is a hero or a villian.
